$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for what a reprobuild release contains.
release.yml reads this file twice: once to build the job matrix, and once,
in the publish job, to compute the exact set of assets that must exist
before anything is made visible. Because both come from here, 'the matrix'
and 'what the release must carry' cannot drift apart -- which is what let
v0.1.0..v0.1.3 each ship a DIFFERENT subset of platforms.
Adding a leg: the bar is a GREEN BUILD OF THIS REPO on that platform, not
'a runner class exists for it'. Since the release is all-or-nothing, a row
that has never produced a binary blocks EVERY release, forever -- it does
not merely miss one asset. A runner that boots and reports its uname
proves the fleet, not the toolchain; get the platform green in ci.yml
first, then add it here. Prove, then gate.
Removing a leg is a deliberate, reviewed act: it narrows what the release
promises. Consumers on a dropped platform then fall back to the
setup-reprobuild source build with a loud warning, instead of downloading
an asset that does not exist. Never remove a leg just to get a red release
green -- fix the leg, or accept and record the narrower promise here.

linux-aarch64: The runner class is real -- eph-linux-arm64 (Tart Linux guest on m3,
maxRunners=3) has executed hundreds of genuine jobs across the workspace.
It is absent for the two reasons that actually matter to an
all-or-nothing release, neither of which is 'does a runner exist':
1. reprobuild has NEVER built on aarch64-linux. Across the workspace,
ci-reprobuild.yml has run 319 jobs on eph-linux-arm64 with ZERO
successes. reprobuild's own ci.yml has no aarch64-linux leg either,
so nothing has entered this flake's devshell on Linux ARM. The
proven set is x86_64-linux and aarch64-darwin.
2. The pool has not scheduled a job since 2026-08-01; jobs queued
against eph-linux-arm64 since then sit with no runner assigned.
Because the release is all-or-nothing, adding this row would make every
release wait out the queue timeout on a platform that has never produced
a binary -- turning 'releases ship a subset' into 'releases never ship'.
flake.nix listing aarch64-linux is what makes this leg look available; a
declared system is not a proven build.
Add the row when a real aarch64-linux build of reprobuild goes green --
the cheap way is an aarch64-linux leg in ci.yml first. Prove, then gate.
darwin-x86_64: No runner exists and none is planned. metacraft-dev-guidelines
policies/ci-workflow-standards.md marks macOS AMD64 'N/A -- no Intel-Mac
runner': the macOS fleet is Apple-silicon only (eph-macos-arm64 on m3).
flake.nix still lists x86_64-darwin among its systems, which is what makes
this leg look available; it is not.
windows-aarch64: A runner DOES exist (eph-win-arm64, m3, qemu-windows-arm + swtpm,
maxRunners=2), so unlike darwin-x86_64 this is blocked by the toolchain,
not the fleet. windows/ensure-clingo.ps1 throws: 'conda-forge publishes
clingo for win-64 only ... A native ARM64 repro.exe cannot load an x64
clingo.dll.' clingo is dlopen'd at module init, so this is fatal, not
degraded. The staged runtime DLLs are x64-specific by name too
(libcrypto-3-x64.dll). Enable this row only after an ARM64 clingo exists;
adding it now would permanently block every release.
